title: Linkability of GPS coordinates in transit
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted in the data flow could be intercepted and linked to the child's identity, potentially revealing the child's location patterns and movement history.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is inferred from LINDDUN Pro methodology; exact node may vary by version.

title: Identification through GPS data sharing
description: The child's device shares live GPS coordinates, which inherently identifies the child's real-time location and movement patterns, enabling identification of the child's whereabouts.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is inferred from LINDDUN Pro methodology; exact node may vary by version.

title: Disclosure of GPS data during transmission
description: GPS coordinates transmitted in the data flow could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive location information.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is inferred from LINDDUN Pro methodology; exact node may vary by version.

title: Excessive storage of GPS data at destination
description: The backend may store GPS coordinates longer than necessary or retain historical location data beyond what is required for the intended purpose, violating data minimization principles.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is inferred from LINDDUN Pro methodology; exact node may vary by version.

title: Unauthorized use of GPS data at destination
description: The backend may use GPS coordinates for purposes beyond what the child expects or consents to, such as third-party tracking, profiling, or sharing with other services.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is inferred from LINDDUN Pro methodology; exact node may vary by version.

title: Linkability of Location Data to Family Members
description: Zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) shared by the Family Account Store can be used to link specific family members to their physical locations and routines, potentially enabling tracking of movement patterns across different contexts.

title: Identification of Family Members via Location Patterns
description: The act of sharing zone definitions at the source can identify family members' locations and daily routines, as home and school zones are inherently tied to specific individuals and their regular activities.

title: Metadata Linkability During Data Transfer
description: Metadata about the data flow (e.g., timestamps, data size, access patterns) could be used to link the zone definitions to specific family members or infer when and how often geofencing checks occur.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: The Geofencing Engine may process or store zone definitions in ways that expose sensitive location information to unauthorized parties, either through improper access controls or unintended data retention.

title: Location-based notifications enable entity linking
description: The geofencing engine shares arrival/departure notifications containing location data, which can be used to link the child entity to the parent entity or other entities in the system based on shared movement patterns.

title: Parent entity can identify child's location patterns
description: The parent external entity receives geofencing notifications that reveal the child entity's movement patterns, enabling identification of the child's location history and behavior.

title: Data in transit can be intercepted
description: The geofencing notifications transmitted from the process to the external entity are in transit and could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to unauthorized disclosure of location data.

title: Location data sharing may violate privacy regulations
description: Sharing geofencing notifications containing location data may violate privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) if proper consent was not obtained from the child entity or if data minimization principles were not followed.

title: Identification of parent and child through personal data
description: The parent provides personally identifiable information (name, date of birth, school) during account registration, which can be used to identify both the parent and the child.

title: Linkability of parent-child data in transit
description: Data transmitted between the parent and the mobile app backend could be intercepted and used to link the parent's identity with the child's profile information.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of personal data
description: The mobile app backend receives and stores sensitive personal data (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) which could be accessed by unauthorized parties if not properly secured.

title: Excessive data collection during registration
description: The registration process may collect more personal data than strictly necessary for account creation and geofence definition, including detailed school information and precise location data.

title: Identity usurpation during account registration
description: During the account registration process, there is a risk that the parent's identity could be stolen or impersonated, allowing unauthorized individuals to create accounts and access child profile information.

title: Non-repudiation of account registration
description: The parent may deny having registered the account or created the child's profile, making it difficult to establish accountability for the data provided.

title: Regulatory non-compliance in data handling
description: The mobile app backend may not comply with data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, COPPA) regarding the collection and storage of children's personal data and geofence information.

title: Implicit Data Disclosure via Stored Personal Data
description: The Family Account & Permissions Store (DS2) receives and stores sensitive personal data including child profiles and geofence zone information. This creates a risk of implicit disclosure where metadata or derived information from stored data could be used to identify or link individuals, even if the explicit data is protected.
assumptions: The data store may retain data longer than necessary, or store metadata that enables re-identification of children and family members.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 from context as it addresses implicit disclosure through metadata/derived data, though the exact threat-tree node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Family Data
description: The data store (DS2) receives and processes personal data including child profiles and geofence zones. If access controls are inadequate, unauthorized parties could access this sensitive family information.
assumptions: The data store may have insufficient access controls or encryption for stored personal data.
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for usurpation at destination; confidence in this classification is high.

title: Excessive Data Collection and Storage
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) shares and stores comprehensive personal data including child profiles and geofence zone data. This may violate the minimality principle by collecting and storing more data than strictly necessary for the intended purpose.
assumptions: The system may collect and store data beyond what is required for family account management and geofencing functionality.
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 applies to explicit disclosure by design; the threat is that the system is designed to store more data than minimally required.

title: Location data in transit could identify child's movements
description: Location data transmitted from parent to backend could be intercepted, revealing the child's current location or movement patterns, potentially identifying the child's whereabouts to unauthorized parties.

title: Location data could be linked to identify child
description: Location data in transit could be correlated with other data sources (e.g., device identifiers, timestamps) to link and identify the child's identity and movements.

title: Backend could disclose location data to unauthorized parties
description: The mobile app backend could improperly disclose the child's location data to unauthorized third parties, violating privacy expectations.

title: Backend may store excessive location data
description: The backend may retain location history longer or with more precision than necessary for the stated purpose, violating data minimization principles.

title: Backend may allow unauthorized access to location data
description: The backend may have insufficient access controls, allowing unauthorized users or processes to access the child's location data.

title: Location History Data in Transit Enables User Identification
description: Location history data transmitted from the DataStore to the Mobile App Backend contains inherently identifiable information about individuals' movements, patterns, and routines. Even without explicit identifiers, the data can be used to identify specific users through their unique movement patterns and temporal data.

title: Location History Data Can Be Linked with Other Data Sources
description: Location history data in transit can potentially be linked with other data sources (e.g., device identifiers, timestamps, app usage data) to create comprehensive user profiles, enabling correlation across different data domains.

title: Location History Data May Be Improperly Disclosed at Destination
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) receives sensitive location history data and may lack adequate access controls, encryption, or audit mechanisms, creating risk of unauthorized disclosure to internal or external parties.

title: Location Data Handling May Violate Privacy Regulations
description: Location history is classified as sensitive personal data under GDPR and similar regulations. The backend's processing and storage of this data must comply with consent requirements, data minimization principles, and user rights, which may not be fully addressed.

title: Location data linkability via metadata
description: Metadata about the source (parent) and destination (secondary guardian) in the location data flow could be used to link the data to specific individuals, potentially revealing the relationship between the parent and the secondary guardian.

title: Child location identifiability through parent's sharing action
description: The parent's act of sharing the child's location data with a secondary guardian creates a privacy risk where the child's location can be identified and tracked by parties beyond the intended recipient.

title: Location data disclosure at backend processing
description: The mobile app backend may store or process the child's location data in a way that exposes it to unauthorized access, internal personnel, or third-party services.

title: Location data linkability during transmission
description: Child's live location data transmitted in transit could be intercepted and linked with other data sources to reconstruct movement patterns and identify the child's routine locations.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location data by guardian
description: Secondary guardian (EE3) may share or disclose the child's live location data to unauthorized third parties, violating the intended privacy scope of the sharing arrangement.

title: Usurpation of location data for unauthorized purposes
description: Secondary guardian may use the child's location data for purposes beyond the authorized scope, such as surveillance, stalking, or other unauthorized monitoring activities.

title: Regulatory non-compliance in external data sharing
description: Backend (P1) may share live location data with external entity (EE3) without proper consent mechanisms or in violation of data protection regulations governing children's location data.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure by Analytics Partner
description: Advertising/analytics partner may store, process, or share the aggregated analytics data beyond the agreed purpose of funding the app's free tier, potentially exposing user engagement patterns to third parties or for undisclosed commercial purposes.

title: Metadata-Based Identification in Transit
description: Metadata about the data flow (e.g., timing, volume, source/destination identifiers) could be used to infer or identify specific users or app instances, even if the payload is aggregated.

title: Misrepresentation of Data Aggregation Level
description: The backend may claim to share 'aggregated' analytics, but if the aggregation is insufficient (e.g., small sample sizes, incomplete anonymization), the data could be re-identified by the partner or third parties.

title: Data Usurpation Beyond Agreed Purpose
description: The analytics partner may use the shared engagement data for purposes beyond funding the free tier, such as building user profiles, targeted advertising, or selling data to other entities without user consent.

title: Location data linkability in transit
description: Location data transmitted in the SOS/check-in message can be linked across time to establish the child's movement patterns and associate with other data sources, potentially revealing sensitive behavioral information.

title: Location sharing enables identification
description: The act of sharing current location data at the source enables identification of the child's whereabouts, which could be used to track movements or infer sensitive activities.

title: Attributable SOS message evidence
description: The SOS message and location data can be attributed to the child, but there is risk of denial or tampering with the evidence of the message's origin and content.

title: Location data disclosure to unauthorized parties
description: The Mobile App Backend receiving the location data may process or store it in ways that could lead to disclosure to unauthorized parties, including third parties or other users.
